status_reasoning: Reviewers explicitly state 'all three reviewers agree that the data set is strong, particularly the diversity of approaches and strong genetic data used to demonstrate that APA-2 and APM-2 are both required for endocytosis.' The demonstration that hemicomplexes remain stable in single mutants is accepted, though reviewers request clarification about 'how much residual AP2 function may exist in the hemi knockouts' for textual clarity, not because they doubt the findings.

The lethality of double mutants and rescue by skin-specific expression is accepted by reviewers as part of the 'strong genetic data.' Reviewers note 'it is unclear why the authors did not report on the electrophysiological signature of the double (alpha/mu) mutant in the skin rescued animals,' indicating they accept the rescue data but want additional characterization, not that they question the finding itself.

The vesicle number reductions in single and double mutants are accepted as part of the strong dataset. Reviewers request that 'p-values for all data upon which arguments or conclusions are based' be included, particularly for 'double mutant phenotypes that appear to trend toward significance,' indicating a need for statistical clarity rather than doubt about the observations themselves.

The presence of large vacuoles and vesicles in mutants is accepted as valid data. Reviewers note these observations are part of the strong dataset and do not challenge the ultrastructural findings, though they suggest contextualizing them with citations to similar phenotypes in other mutants.

Reviewers explicitly challenge the interpretation of vesicle size data, stating 'Does the defect in vesicle size imply a role for determining the size of the vesicle? Many endocytic mutations alter vesicle size and it is unlikely that all participate in the control of vesicle diameter. An alternative conclusion is that any mutation that disrupts the fidelity of endocytosis may well disrupt the ability to reliably generate small vesicles of a consistent size.' They also note similarities to synaptotagmin mutants should be cited, suggesting the interpretation is overreaching.

While reviewers accept the cargo mislocalization data as part of the strong dataset, they suggest additional experiments 'could persuasively show that in mutants lacking specific subunits, the remaining AP2 subunits have the capacity to function as hemi-complexes' using tyrosine-based motifs. The suggestion that these experiments 'would significantly strengthen the manuscript' implies the current cargo data, while supportive, leaves some uncertainty about the hemicomplex model's full scope.

Reviewers explicitly state 'it is not possible, at the light level, to know whether an altered axon/synapse ratio of protein distribution has anything to do with the recycling of individual proteins. This should be discussed.' This directly challenges the interpretation that accumulation of synaptic vesicle proteins in axons reflects endocytic defects, indicating the evidence is insufficient to support the claim without additional discussion of limitations.

The electrophysiological data is accepted as part of the strong dataset. Reviewers request p-values be included 'when discussing comparisons being made regarding electrophysiological data' for clarity, not because they question the findings. They also note 'synaptic vesicle endocytosis is never directly assayed in the current study' and suggest citing synaptotagmin work, but this is contextual rather than challenging the electrophysiology results themselves.

The core hemicomplex model is strongly supported by reviewers who state the manuscript demonstrates 'that APA-2 and APM-2 are both required for endocytosis' with 'strong genetic data.' Reviewers request discussion of 'the contribution of hemi-complex function to the wild type animal' and note that 'protein abundance for the residual hemi-complex is relatively low,' but these are requests for contextual discussion rather than challenges to the model itself.

The reduced stability of hemicomplexes in single mutants is accepted as valid data. Reviewers request clarification about 'how much residual AP2 function may exist' and note that 'protein abundance for the residual hemi-complex is relatively low,' but these comments seek textual clarity about the implications rather than challenging the biochemical measurements themselves.

Reviewers explicitly request that 'the authors should reference the mammalian work showing that loss of mu2 leads to loss of alpha and point out that this is in contrast to the findings in this system.' This indicates they accept the contrast between C. elegans and mammalian systems as valid and want it highlighted, not questioned.

The observation that double mutants retain functional synapses and that AP2-independent mechanisms exist is accepted as part of the strong dataset. Reviewers note 'synaptic vesicle endocytosis is never directly assayed' and suggest citing similar phenotypes, but these are contextual comments rather than challenges to the finding that vesicles are still generated in AP2 mutants.
